# Introduction

The best way to learn data analysis is to study examples, so these lessons
build small versions of real analysis pipelines, each of a different kind.
This lesson defines what a pipeline is (ingest, clean, explore, model,
communicate) and introduces the course's two running examples, which share the
same data shapes so that every lesson works against either:

-   Disaster management: a volunteer group coordinating response to
    storms, floods, and other local disasters (for software-oriented learners).
-   Ecological data collection: a field survey recording organisms and
    environmental conditions at study sites (for science-oriented learners).
-   A data analysis pipeline is a chain of small, checkable steps.
-   There are many kinds of analysis; this course samples them rather than
    drilling one.
-   We use mature tools (Polars, DuckDB, Vega-Altair, httpx) instead of
    building our own.
-   Reproducibility means recording every step so an analysis can be re-run
    and audited.
